concepts.learning_objective: Define the production function as the maximum output obtainable from given inputs and use it to compute output.
Explain that a production function assumes efficient use of inputs and is defined for a given technology.

topics.title: The Short Run, the Long Run and Isoquants

concepts.learning_objective: Distinguish the short run from the long run by whether all inputs can be varied.
Explain an isoquant and why it slopes downward when marginal products are positive.

topics.title: Total Product, Average Product and Marginal Product

concepts.learning_objective: Define total, average and marginal product of a variable input.
Calculate TP, AP and MP schedules from one another.

topics.title: Law of Variable Proportions and Shapes of Product Curves

concepts.learning_objective: State and explain the law of variable proportions using changing factor proportions.
Explain the shapes of the TP, AP and MP curves and the relationship between AP and MP.
Distinguish constant, increasing and decreasing returns to scale.
Identify returns to scale of a Cobb-Douglas production function from the sum of its exponents.

topics.title: Cost Function and Short Run Cost Concepts

concepts.learning_objective: Explain the cost function as the least cost of producing each output level.
Calculate TFC, TVC, TC, AFC, AVC, SAC and SMC and relate them to one another.

topics.title: Shapes of the Short Run Cost Curves

concepts.learning_objective: Describe the shapes of the TFC and AFC curves and why AFC is a rectangular hyperbola.
Explain why SMC, AVC and SAC are U-shaped and where SMC cuts AVC and SAC.
Define long run average and marginal cost and explain why there is no fixed cost in the long run.
Relate the U-shape of the LRAC curve to increasing, constant and decreasing returns to scale.
